title: ICYM2I: The illusion of multimodal informativeness under missingness
one_liner: Estimate the value of an extra modality only after correcting for which examples are missing that modality, because missingness can bias the apparent gain.
lead: Adding another modality can look useful in training data and disappoint in deployment. The reason is simple: the cases where a modality is present are often not a random slice of the world. This paper shows that you can overestimate the value of a modality unless you correct for who is missing it and why.

problem.h2: Why extra modalities can look better than they are
paras: Suppose a system can use text alone or text plus another modality. If the added modality is usually present on easier or more carefully collected cases, then a model that uses it may appear stronger for the wrong reason, because the evaluation set is tilted toward cases where that modality was available.

This matters when the source setting and the target setting lose modalities in different ways. A model may seem to gain a lot from the added modality during development and gain much less after deployment because the missingness pattern changed.

callout.html: Correct the evaluation by reweighting examples according to how likely their modality pattern is, so the estimated value of an extra modality reflects the target setting rather than a biased observed slice.

panels.title: 1. Train with many complete cases

panels.title: 2. Deployment loses some modalities

panels.title: 3. Naive comparison is biased

panels.title: 5. Estimate true target value

steps.text: For each example, record the missingness pattern.

steps.b: Estimate how likely each pattern is
steps.text: Model the chance that an example appears with a given set of observed modalities.
Give more weight to examples whose pattern is underrepresented, because those cases would otherwise be drowned out.

steps.b: Compare models under the weighted view
steps.text: Recompute predictive performance and modality value with the corrected weights.
Estimate how much the extra modality helps in the target setting by comparing models under corrected weights rather than under the biased observed sample.

paras: The paper changes the evaluation rule. Instead of comparing multimodal and single-modality models on the raw observed sample, it compares them on a reweighted sample that accounts for missingness because raw observation can favor the cases where a modality happened to be present.

hidden.name: missingness bias
paras: The hidden quantity is the gap between the apparent value of an extra modality in observed data and its true value in the target setting. This gap appears when modality presence is linked to case difficulty, collection practice, or device availability, because then the observed complete cases no longer represent the target population fairly.
ICYM2I estimates and corrects this gap with inverse-probability weights. Rare or undersampled missingness patterns receive more weight so the final estimate reflects the setting you care about.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark modality patterns that need larger correction weights because they are underrepresented.

reads.html: The question is not only whether another modality helps, but whether it helps after you correct for who actually had that modality available, because raw observation can favor easy fully observed cases.
Inverse-probability weighting corrects the observed sample so estimated information gain is tied to the target missingness process.

paras: Bias enters when complete cases are easier, cleaner, or otherwise different from incomplete cases. A raw average then gives too much influence to those complete cases, so the measured value of the added modality can be inflated.

Reweighting fixes that by undoing the sampling tilt. An example that rarely appears with its observed modality pattern gets more weight because one such example stands in for many similar target cases that were not fully observed.

After reweighting, a model only looks better if it truly helps across the corrected target population. That makes the reported information gain more trustworthy because the estimate is tied to the deployment missingness pattern rather than to the convenience sample seen during collection.

stages.s: examples with observed and missing modalities

math.words: Each example gets weight one over the chance of its observed missingness pattern, so rare observed patterns count more in the final average.
symbols: which modalities are present for that example
how often that pattern appears under the missingness process
the correction weight used in evaluation

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose complete cases appear only 20 percent of the time in the target setting.
A complete case then gets weight 1 / 0.20 = 5.
A common text-only case that appears 50 percent of the time gets weight 1 / 0.50 = 2.
The complete case counts more because it stands in for more target cases than the raw sample suggests.

math.note: The exact missingness model can vary, but the correction idea stays the same: downweight overrepresented patterns and upweight underrepresented ones.

charts.title: Naive modality gain estimate
charts.note: This can mislead because the observed sample may favor cases with extra modalities.

charts.title: ICYM2I corrected estimate
charts.note: This improves the estimate because missingness correction ties the comparison to the cases that matter in deployment.

items.b: Missingness probabilities may be estimated poorly.
items.html: If the missingness model is wrong, the weights can be wrong too, so the correction may still be biased.

items.b: Very rare patterns can create unstable weights.
items.html: When one pattern is extremely rare, its weight can become very large, which increases variance because a few examples carry too much influence.

items.b: Unrecorded causes of missingness may remain.
items.html: If important drivers of missingness are absent from the data, correction can only go so far because the model cannot adjust for causes it never sees.
The method is most useful when you can model missingness well because then the corrected estimate separates true modality value from collection bias.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Create a dataset where an extra modality is more likely to be present on easier examples. Compare the raw measured gain from adding that modality against the corrected gain from ICYM2I.

Then change the target missingness pattern and repeat the comparison. The corrected estimate should track the new target setting more closely because it accounts for how modality availability changes across environments.
demo.closing: The demo should show that a modality can look highly useful in raw observed data and much less useful after missingness correction.
